verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time, members of the recovery team... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'NASA's Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. ET on Friday, April 10, 2026'; R3: 'Splashdown occurred April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)... Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R4: 'The Orion capsule safely splashed down at 8:07 p.m. ET... off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm the exact location, date, time in ET, and safe splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew returned to Earth after a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: implies 10 days (April 1 launch to April 10 splashdown); R2: 'concluding a successful 10-day journey'; R3: 'Mission duration 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R4: 'ending the record-breaking 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state '10-day mission'; R3 precise duration is ~9.06 days but consistent with common rounding from April 1-10/11.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft landed safely in the water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'successful conclusion... splashdown'; R2: 'Orion spacecraft splashed down... successfully'; R3: 'Splashdown occurred... U.S. Navy recovered the crew'; R4: 'Orion capsule landed... picture-perfect ending'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm safe water landing (splashdown) of Orion.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II landing occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... on Friday'; R2: 'at 8:07 p.m. ET on Friday, April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: R1 and R2 directly state Friday, April 10, 2026; others align with date.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II landing location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'waters off San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California'; R3: 'Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R4: 'off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All references specify Pacific Ocean near/off/southwest of San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration was approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day journey'; R3: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds'; R4: '10-day mission'; R1: April 1 to April 10 (~10 days)
verifications.reasoning: 'Approximately' matches all; R3 precise ~9 days but sources round to 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II mission began on April 1'; R2: 'The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026'; R3: 'Launch date April 1, 2026'

verifications.claim: Artemis II was a crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'human spaceflight around the moon... swung around the moon’s far side'; R2: 'carrying a crew of four astronauts around the Moon'; R3: 'Crewed lunar flyby... first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17'
verifications.reasoning: All describe as crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: Artemis II involved no lunar landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lunar flyby... sets up... put American back on the surface of the moon in 2028'; R2: 'around the Moon'; R3: 'Crewed lunar flyby... test flight supporting the Artemis IV mission to return humans to the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm flyby/orbit, no landing; future missions for landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tested systems for future landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check out key systems of Orion... demonstrated that their Orion spacecraft can handle transporting human beings to the moon... sets up the next steps... land on the moon'; R3: 'validate the Orion spacecraft's systems... ahead of sustained lunar exploration... supporting the Artemis IV mission to return humans to the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports testing Orion/systems for future lunar landings.

verifications.claim: Following the splashdown, the Artemis II crew was extracted by NASA and U.S. Navy personnel for transport back to land.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team... U.S.S. John P. Murtha... hoisted them up for hovering helicopters'; R2: 'recovery teams work to secure... helicopter prepares to lift the Artemis II crew'; R3: 'U.S. Navy recovered the crew... helicopters transported the astronauts to the USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'U.S. Navy divers... hoisted into helicopters... to the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm NASA/Navy extraction via divers/boats/helicopters to ship.
